paragraphs.text: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to reports cited by TechCrunch, Fortune and The Motley Fool. The price sits above the range of $70 to $78 a share that the company set when it began marketing the deal to investors the week before.

At $83 a share, Anthropic is valued at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19, under the ticker ANT. The company itself had not confirmed the final share count or the total amount raised when the reports were published.

Anthropic had planned to sell about 825 million shares, roughly 801 million of them new shares from the company and the rest from existing holders, according to The Motley Fool. At that size and an $83 price, the sale would bring in about $68.5 billion. Fortune, citing Bloomberg, reported that the offering was increased because of strong demand, but the size of the increase was not disclosed.

Alongside the public sale, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares in a private placement, TechCrunch reported. The Motley Fool noted that, counting that placement, Anthropic's total fundraising would top the roughly $75 billion that SpaceX raised in its record-setting IPO in June, although the public portion alone at the original size would fall slightly short of it.
Founders sell, big tech keeps large stakes

Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders, including chief executive Dario Amodei, sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the offering, according to TechCrunch. At the IPO price, that comes to about $282 million per founder.

Amazon owns nearly 15 percent of the company and Google almost 14 percent, together close to 30 percent, TechCrunch reported. No venture capital investor holds more than 5 percent. Sequoia, former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt and Singapore's GIC each hold about 1 percent, and several large investment firms, including Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel and Altimeter, reportedly planned to buy billions of dollars of shares in the IPO.

The valuation compares with $965 billion in Anthropic's last private funding round in May, when it raised $65 billion. TechCrunch also reported that the company had been aiming for a valuation of $2 trillion several months earlier. OpenAI, its closest rival, was last reported to be valued at $1.25 trillion and has not announced plans to go public.

The price above the range points to strong demand for one of the few large AI model makers that public investors can buy directly. It also puts a market value on Anthropic above the last reported private value of OpenAI, a reversal for a company that was long seen as the smaller of the two. Large stakes held by Amazon and Google mean two cloud providers will remain among its most important shareholders after the listing.

The first trades of ANT on the Nasdaq on November 19 will show whether public investors value Anthropic as highly as the IPO buyers did, and the company's final filing should confirm how many shares were sold.
